A tiny suited miner braces against the rock face with a cutting-tool, sparks washing over their scarred orange suit, dwarfed by the floodlit cliff.
A crew of small figures works along a gantry high on the structure, their helmet-lamps a string of sparks against the dark machinery.
A foreman stands silhouetted in a floodlit hatchway, waving a hauler in with glowing light-wands, tiny against the looming rig.
An EVA team hauls a cable hand-over-hand across open rock, four suited figures strung along the line like beads, the asteroid curving away beneath them.
A lone worker rides a maintenance pod along the underside of the processing hull, one hand gripping the rail, legs dangling in the dark.
A pair of miners crouch over a massive valve fitting, wrenches leveraged against the flange, their boots magnetized to the pitted grey surface.
A single miner trudges a narrow catwalk between two reactor housings, hard-hat lamp cutting the exhaust haze, lunch-pail swinging at their side.
A suited figure stands at the base of a drill-head three stories tall, clipboard raised, utterly swallowed by the machine above them.
A worker perches on a ore-chute lip, guiding a conveyor coupling into place with both hands, the chute mouth wide enough to swallow a truck.
Two figures in patched suits share a thermos on a girder ledge, the vast dark of the mining pit dropping away behind them.
A rigger hangs in a harness against the side of the extraction tower, welding torch flaring, the structure stretching far above and below.
A small crew pushes a pallet of drill-bits across the rock floor by hand, leaning hard, the load nearly as tall as they are.
A figure in a faded yellow suit crouches inside an open equipment bay, half-swallowed by the machinery, only their boots visible from outside.
A shift supervisor points a clipboard at a junior miner on a catwalk, both of them tiny specks against the corrugated bulk of the ore-sorter.
A worker signals a crane operator from the rock floor below, arms raised, the crane hook descending on a cable thicker than their body.
An EVA miner clips a tether to a rock-anchor bolt, the asteroid surface dropping away in a long curve, nothing else visible for kilometers.
A three-person crew patches a pressure seal on a pipeline junction, kneeling in the grit, their suit patches color-coded for different repair crews.
A lone figure stands atop a dormant drill-platform watching a hauler rise into the black, their helmet visor catching the thruster bloom.
A worker in a scuffed red suit stencils a section number on a rock wall with a spray-gun, the tunnel stretching endlessly behind them.
A miner eats a ration block inside a pressurized bubble-shelter, suit half-unsealed, the vast excavation pit visible through the scratched dome above.
Two figures wrestle a replacement drill-bit into a carousel magazine, grunting against the inertia, the bit taller than either of them suited up.
A safety inspector with a sensor wand moves along a pipe rack, checking joints one by one, their orange vest bright in the floodlights.
A small group of miners waits at an airlock cycling light, helmets on, tools clipped to belts, ready for the next shift underground.
A miner on a cherry-picker platform rises slowly past the flank of a parked hauler the size of a building, checking hull plating seams.
A figure kneels at the edge of a bore-hole wide enough to drop a house into, lowering a sensor package on a cable by hand.
